# https://bestbuyincentives.com/vacation-certificates
BB BestBuy Incentives Incentives Industries Case Studies Resources Sales Resources FAQ About Programs Vacation Certificate Programs Vacation Certificates Travel Certificates Vacation Incentives Travel Incentive Programs Sales Incentive Programs Compare Travel incentives vs. Discounting Travel incentives vs. Gift Cards Travel incentives vs. Cash Rebates Book a Call → Home Programs Vacation Certificates That Close High-Ticket Sales A vacation certificate is a value-added reward you hand a qualified buyer at the close. It gives your representative something exciting to talk about instead of another price cut, and it protects the margin you worked to build. By Karl Kramer , CEO of Best Buy Incentives Published August 26, 2026 Book a Strategy Call What a vacation certificate is A vacation certificate is a discounted travel voucher your business gives a customer when they complete a qualifying purchase. It entitles the recipient to a resort stay, a cruise getaway, or a city escape from a curated set of destinations. For your sales team, it is a simple, tangible reward that makes the offer more memorable and gives the buyer a reason to say yes today. You are not selling a vacation. You are selling your product, and the certificate is the added value that tips a hesitant buyer into a decision. Why a trip out-closes a discount of the same cost A discount lowers your price permanently and trains buyers to negotiate. A vacation certificate carries a perceived value far higher than what the program costs your business, because a resort stay or cruise feels like an experience, not a line item. The buyer pictures the destination. That emotional pull is what moves a stalled deal. The margin math is straightforward. A price cut comes straight off your profit on every unit. A certificate is a fixed, predictable program cost that you control, so you can add excitement at the close without eroding the number that matters. The destinations your customers can choose Programs such as Enjoy a Great Escape and Enjoy a Paradise Escape let recipients pick from resort stays, cruise getaways, and popular city destinations. The variety is part of the appeal. A buyer who loves the beach and a buyer who wants a cruise both see something they want, which keeps the reward relevant across your whole customer base. How a representative presents it at the close Timing is everything. Your representative confirms the product is a fit, handles any real objection, and only then introduces the certificate as the reason to move forward now. Presented after value is established, the certificate adds urgency and excitement rather than looking like a bribe. See how the program works and the exact training script reps follow. Which industries use vacation certificates Sales teams across many high-ticket verticals use this at the close: Automotive dealerships Jewelry stores Furniture retailers Home improvement and HVAC Boat and RV dealers Roofing contractors Wedding and event businesses Marketing agencies that run campaigns for these clients Results sales teams report On our documented case studies , teams report a stronger close rate, a higher average ticket, and more referrals once a compelling reward enters the conversation. Because the reward is added value rather than a price cut, the extra revenue lands with the margin intact. [METHODOLOGY LINE: Jed and Karl to supply the exact wording. Placeholder: Figures are aggregated from client-reported results across Best Buy Incentives programs, 1992 to 2026, and are averages, not guarantees.] How to launch a vacation certificate program Getting started is fast. A short call defines your goal, your qualifying purchase threshold, and the destinations that fit your buyers. Most teams are live within days, not months. Your representatives receive a simple script and a one-page overview, and a dedicated travel support team handles every booking so your people stay focused on selling. When you are ready, book a strategy call and we will map a program to your sales floor. You can also read how the program works and review the sales-team training script your reps will use. Frequently asked questions What is a vacation certificate? It is a discounted travel voucher a business gives a customer after a qualifying purchase. It entitles the recipient to a resort stay, cruise, or city getaway from a curated set of destinations, and it is used as a value-added closing tool. How is a vacation certificate different from a discount? A discount lowers your price and reduces margin on every sale. A vacation certificate is a fixed program cost that adds perceived value at the close, so you protect price while still giving the buyer a reason to act. Do my representatives need training? Very little. Reps receive a short script and a one-page overview. The key is timing: present the certificate after the product fit is confirmed, as the reason to move forward now. How fast can we launch? Most teams are live within days. A short call defines your goal, qualifying threshold, and destinations, and a travel support team handles redemption from there. Who handles the travel booking? A dedicated travel support team manages every booking, so your sales team never touches travel logistics and stays focused on selling. BB BestBuy Incentives Incentives Industries Case Studies Resources Sales Resources FAQ About Programs Vacation Certificate Programs Vacation Certificates Travel Certificates Vacation Incentives Travel Incentive Programs Sales Incentive Programs Compare Travel incentives vs. Discounting Travel incentives vs. Gift Cards Travel incentives vs. Cash Rebates Book a Call → Home Programs Travel Certificates Your Sales Team Can Offer Instead of a Discount A travel certificate is a business tool: a discounted travel voucher your team offers at the close so the buyer gets added value and you keep your price. It replaces the reflex to discount with a reason to decide. By Karl Kramer , CEO of Best Buy Incentives Published August 26, 2026 Book a Strategy Call What travel certificates are, in plain terms A travel certificate, also called a travel incentive certificate, is a discounted travel voucher a business provides to a customer who completes a qualifying purchase. It gives the recipient a resort stay, cruise, or getaway from a set list of destinations. For the business, it is a repeatable, budgetable way to reward buyers and differentiate the offer. Why travel certificates beat a price cut Buyers remember experiences. A travel certificate carries perceived value well above its program cost, so it moves deals that a matching discount would not. And unlike a discount, it does not reset the buyer's expectation of your price on the next purchase. You protect both this sale and the next one. For a full comparison, see travel incentives versus discounting and travel incentives versus gift cards . The destinations on offer Certificates draw from programs like Enjoy a Great Escape and Enjoy a Paradise Escape, covering resort stays, cruise getaways, and city escapes. A curated range keeps the reward exciting for a wide mix of customers. Presenting a travel certificate at the close Confirm fit first. Resolve the genuine objection. Then present the travel certificate as the value that makes acting now the better choice. This sequence keeps the certificate positive and persuasive. Reps use the training script , and you can review how the program works . Which industries use travel certificates Sales teams across many high-ticket verticals use this at the close: Automotive dealerships Jewelry stores Furniture retailers Home improvement and HVAC Boat and RV dealers Roofing contractors Wedding and event businesses Marketing agencies that run campaigns for these clients Results sales teams report On our documented case studies , teams report a stronger close rate, a higher average ticket, and more referrals once a compelling reward enters the conversation. Because the reward is added value rather than a price cut, the extra revenue lands with the margin intact. [METHODOLOGY LINE: Jed and Karl to supply the exact wording. Placeholder: Figures are aggregated from client-reported results across Best Buy Incentives programs, 1992 to 2026, and are averages, not guarantees.] How to launch travel certificates Getting started is fast. A short call defines your goal, your qualifying purchase threshold, and the destinations that fit your buyers. Most teams are live within days, not months. Your representatives receive a simple script and a one-page overview, and a dedicated travel support team handles every booking so your people stay focused on selling. When you are ready, book a strategy call and we will map a program to your sales floor. You can also read how the program works and review the sales-team training script your reps will use. Frequently asked questions What is a travel certificate for business? It is a discounted travel voucher a business gives a customer after a qualifying purchase, used as a value-added reward at the close to protect price and lift close rate. Are travel certificates the same as gift cards? No. A gift card has a fixed, known dollar value. A travel certificate carries perceived value far above its program cost because it represents an experience, which makes it more persuasive at the close. Can we set the qualifying purchase amount? Yes. You define the qualifying threshold so the certificate is only offered on sales that justify the program cost. How quickly can we start? Most teams launch within days after a short setup call that defines the goal, threshold, and destinations. Who supports redemption? A dedicated travel support team handles every booking, so your representatives never manage travel logistics. Related reading What Is a Customer Purchase Incentive? Frequently asked questions What is a sales incentive program? A structured way to reward qualifying customer purchases with a discounted travel voucher, used to close more deals while protecting price and margin. What are customer purchase incentives? Value-added rewards given to a customer for completing a qualifying purchase. Here, the incentive is a discounted travel voucher redeemable for a resort stay, cruise, or getaway. Will this replace discounting entirely? It gives reps a stronger alternative to discounting. Most teams cut how often they discount because the incentive gives buyers a reason to act without a price concession. How fast can we launch? # https://bestbuyincentives.com/faq
BB BestBuy Incentives Incentives Industries Case Studies Resources Sales Resources FAQ About Programs Vacation Certificate Programs Vacation Certificates Travel Certificates Vacation Incentives Travel Incentive Programs Sales Incentive Programs Compare Travel incentives vs. Discounting Travel incentives vs. Gift Cards Travel incentives vs. Cash Rebates Book a Call → Frequently asked questions Everything sales leaders ask us. Straight answers on how the programs work, what they cost, whether they're legit, and how fast you can put a closing tool on your sales floor. The Basics What is BestBuyIncentives? BestBuyIncentives is a sales-growth company operated by Karl Kramer & Company, Inc., in business since 1992. It helps high-ticket sales teams use discounted travel vouchers as customer-facing closing tools that can add value without automatically cutting price. What is a travel incentive certificate? A travel incentive certificate is a vacation reward you give a customer as part of closing a sale. It carries a perceived value far higher than its cost to you, so it motivates a buying decision while protecting your margin. The customer redeems the trip directly through a dedicated travel support team — your reps never handle logistics. How do sales incentive programs work? You buy certificates in bulk, then your reps offer one to close or upsell a deal (for example, 'buy today and enjoy a complimentary getaway'). The customer accepts, you close at full price, and the customer books their vacation directly with the travel team. It replaces discounting with an experience buyers actually get excited about. How is this different from a gift card? Gift cards have a known, fixed dollar value that buyers mentally deduct from your price. A vacation carries a perceived value many times its cost, so a memorable trip closes deals a small gift card never will — and it protects your margin instead of eroding it. Is this the same as offering a discount? No — it's the opposite. Discounting comes straight off your gross margin and trains buyers to wait for the next price cut. A travel incentive adds perceived value on top of your offer, so you hold your price, protect profit, and still give the customer a reason to say yes now. Results & ROI Can discounted travel vouchers help increase close rates? Yes. Teams using BestBuyIncentives report an average close-rate lift of about 37%. Instead of negotiating on price, reps hand the buyer a compelling reason to act, which shortens the sales cycle and increases the percentage of deals that close. How much can a travel incentive increase my sales? Results vary by team and offer, but clients typically see three things move at once: higher close rate (about 37% on average), higher average ticket, and more referrals. Because you stop discounting, that added revenue lands with your margin intact. Use the ROI calculator on our site to model your own numbers. How can discounted travel vouchers help protect profit margin? A 10% discount on a 30%-margin product wipes out roughly a third of your profit on that deal. A travel incentive costs you a small fraction of the deal it closes while the customer perceives it as high value — so you keep your price and your margin while still winning the sale. Pricing & Terms How much does a discounted travel voucher cost? Certificates are priced for bulk deployment, so the per-certificate cost is a small fraction of the deal it helps close. Exact pricing depends on volume and program — book a quick call for a custom quote. A monthly subscription unlocks even deeper discounts. Is there a minimum order or subscription? Certificates can be issued on demand, and you can lock in deeper pricing with a monthly subscription. There's no complicated commitment to get started — we'll recommend the volume and structure that fits your sales floor on a short strategy call. Can I use a certificate for myself? Absolutely, yes. Reward yourself with a vacation and enjoy all the same benefits your customers do. Trust & Legitimacy Are these travel incentives legitimate, or is it a scam? They're legitimate. BestBuyIncentives has operated since 1992 and has served 1,200+ sales teams. Resorts and travel providers offer these stays to fill availability and earn word-of-mouth exposure, and a trained travel support team handles every booking, so both you and your customers are taken care of. How are these travel offers even possible? Resorts want to fill unsold room nights and love the organic exposure guests create by sharing their trips. That makes offering discounted or complimentary stays a win for the resort, a win for your customer, and a win for you as the business giving the reward. How long has BestBuyIncentives been in business? Since 1992. It's operated by Karl Kramer & Company, Inc. (Bellmore, NY) and has helped more than 1,200 sales teams close more business with incentives instead of discounts. The Customer Experience What is the customer's experience like? Customers book their vacation directly with a highly trained, courteous travel support team that goes out of its way to give every guest an excellent experience. You never handle the logistics — your only job is to hand over the certificate and close the deal. How do customers use their discounted travel voucher? The customer follows the simple instructions on their certificate and books directly with the travel support team, choosing their dates and destination from the available options. Everything after you hand over the certificate is handled for them. Do my reps need training to use this? Experienced representatives may already know how to present a customer incentive, and the program includes guidance so the team can explain the discounted travel voucher accurately. Getting Started What types of businesses use travel incentives? High-ticket and high-consideration sales teams — including auto dealerships, jewelers, furniture retailers, home-improvement companies, e-commerce retailers, travel clubs, health clubs, employee-rewards programs, luxury retail, and B2B sales organizations — where protecting margin and standing out beats competing on price. # https://bestbuyincentives.com/travel-incentives-vs-discounting
BB BestBuy Incentives Incentives Industries Case Studies Resources Sales Resources FAQ About Programs Vacation Certificate Programs Vacation Certificates Travel Certificates Vacation Incentives Travel Incentive Programs Sales Incentive Programs Compare Travel incentives vs. Discounting Travel incentives vs. Gift Cards Travel incentives vs. Cash Rebates Book a Call → Head to head Travel incentives vs. discounting. When you cut price to win a deal, the profit comes straight out of your pocket. Here's exactly how a travel incentive beats a discount on every dimension that matters to a high-ticket sales team. Discounting Travel Incentive Effect on gross margin Comes straight off profit — a 10% cut on a 30%-margin product erases about a third of that deal's profit. Costs a small fraction of the deal it closes. Your price — and your margin — stay intact. Close rate Buyers still hesitate, and price cuts quickly become expected on every deal. Gives the buyer a compelling reason to act now — teams report an average close-rate lift of about 37%. Perceived value vs. your cost 1:1 — a $200 price cut costs you the full $200. Roughly 10:1 — the vacation's perceived value far exceeds what it costs you. Word of mouth & referrals Nobody tells their friends about a discount. Guests post about and talk up their vacation — free exposure that drives new business. Brand positioning Trains your market to wait for the next sale and compete on price. Positions you on experience and value — impossible to compare on a spreadsheet. Repeat & loyalty Erodes price integrity and conditions one-time bargain hunters. A memorable reward builds loyalty and brings customers back. Who handles fulfillment Not applicable. A dedicated travel support team handles every booking — your team does nothing. The discount math A 10% discount on a 30%-margin product wipes out about a third of your profit on that deal. And once you discount, buyers expect it next time. You've trained your market to wait for the price to drop. The incentive math A vacation's perceived value runs about 10x what it costs you — and your price never moves. Higher close rate, higher average ticket, and more referrals — all with your margin intact. The bottom line Stop discounting. Start closing. Is it better to offer a discount or a travel incentive? A travel incentive almost always wins. Discounting comes directly off your margin and trains buyers to wait for the next price cut, while a travel incentive adds high perceived value on top of your offer, so you hold your price and still give the customer a reason to say yes now. Why do travel incentives close more deals than discounts? Because a vacation carries a perceived value many times its cost and creates an emotional reason to buy today, whereas a discount is simply expected and negotiated. Teams using travel incentives report an average close-rate lift of about 37%. Does offering a discounted travel voucher hurt my margin? The voucher may cost less than a comparable cash discount, allowing the business to preserve more of the core price. Compare the exact voucher cost, discount pattern, close rate, cancellations, and gross profit before deciding. See what stopping the discount does to your numbers. # https://bestbuyincentives.com/travel-incentives-vs-gift-cards
BB BestBuy Incentives Incentives Industries Case Studies Resources Sales Resources FAQ About Programs Vacation Certificate Programs Vacation Certificates Travel Certificates Vacation Incentives Travel Incentive Programs Sales Incentive Programs Compare Travel incentives vs. Discounting Travel incentives vs. Gift Cards Travel incentives vs. Cash Rebates Book a Call → Head to head Travel incentives vs. gift cards. A gift card is practical but forgettable, and its value comes straight out of your pocket. A vacation costs you far less than buyers think it's worth — and it's something they actually get excited about. Gift Cards Travel Incentive Perceived value vs. your cost 1:1 — a $100 card feels like $100 and costs you $100. Roughly 10:1 — a getaway feels far more valuable than it costs you. Emotional pull Useful, but rarely exciting or memorable. A dream vacation people look forward to, talk about, and remember. Effect on gross margin Full face value comes straight out of your profit. Costs a small fraction of the deal it helps close. Word of mouth & referrals Gift cards are rarely shared or talked about. Guests post about and recommend their trip — free exposure. Brand positioning A commodity reward any competitor can match. Differentiates you on experience, not on who gives the bigger card. Leftover value Partial use, forgotten balances, and re-gifting. A complete experience that gets fully redeemed and enjoyed. Who handles fulfillment You buy, distribute, and track balances. A dedicated travel support team handles every booking. The gift-card math A gift card feels worth exactly its face value — and costs you every dollar of it. It's a practical thank-you, not a reason to buy today, so it rarely moves a hesitant deal over the line. The incentive math A vacation's perceived value runs about 10x its cost — and it creates real excitement. That excitement is what closes the deal, protects your margin, and earns referrals a gift card never will. The bottom line Stop discounting. Start closing. Are travel incentives better than gift cards for closing sales? Yes. A gift card carries a fixed, known value that costs you dollar for dollar, while a travel incentive has a perceived value many times its cost and creates genuine excitement — which is what actually motivates a buying decision. Why does a vacation outperform a gift card of the same cost? Because buyers judge a reward by how it makes them feel. A card is practical and forgettable; a vacation is aspirational and memorable, so it drives more closes, more referrals, and more loyalty for the same or lower cost. Do gift cards hurt my margin more than a travel incentive? Generally yes — the gift card's full face value comes out of your profit, whereas a travel certificate costs only a fraction of the deal it helps you close. A cash rebate is just a discount in disguise — it comes straight off your margin and trains buyers to chase money back. A vacation costs you far less and gives customers something to get excited about. Cash Rebates Travel Incentive Effect on gross margin Cash back is a direct discount — the full amount comes off your profit. Costs a small fraction of the deal; your margin stays intact. Perceived value vs. your cost Exactly its dollar amount — no more. Roughly 10x its cost in perceived value. Emotional pull Treated as money owed, not a reward. An aspirational experience that motivates action. Buyer behavior Trains customers to hold out for cash back. Keeps the conversation on value, not price. Word of mouth & referrals Nobody tells their friends about a rebate. Vacations get shared and drive new referrals. Redemption experience Forms, delays, processing — and breakage. Simple redemption handled by the travel support team. Brand positioning Signals you compete on price. Positions you on experience and value. The rebate math A cash rebate is a discount with extra steps — every dollar comes off your margin. It's expected, negotiated, and forgotten the moment it's spent, so it does little to differentiate you. The incentive math A vacation's perceived value runs about 10x its cost — and your price never drops. You protect margin, stand out on experience, and earn the referrals a rebate never generates. The bottom line Stop discounting. Start closing. Is a travel incentive better than a cash rebate? Yes. A cash rebate is effectively a discount — its full value comes off your margin and buyers treat it as money owed. A travel incentive costs a fraction of the deal, carries far higher perceived value, and creates excitement that closes sales. Why do cash rebates hurt margin more than travel incentives? A rebate pays out its full dollar amount straight from your profit, while a travel certificate costs only a small fraction of the deal it helps close — so the incentive protects margin the rebate erodes. How does cash back compare with a discounted travel voucher? Cash back has a fixed dollar value and directly reduces economics. A discounted travel voucher can be more memorable, but only when the customer values it and understands all recipient costs, deadlines, availability, and restrictions.
